title: Initial Rapid Pathology Assessment of Kidney Tissue
author: Jamie Allen
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bt8gnrtw
materials: Tissue is embedded in protocol: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.br4fm8tn
Section samples at 5 µm on a microtome.
PAS stain tissue sections with protocol: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.buaknscw

steps.title: Scan slides and save images
steps.instruction: Use a Leica brightfield slide scanner to scan each kidney slide and save the resulting image files as either .tiff or .jpg format.

steps.title: Import images into QuPath
steps.instruction: Open QuPath software and load the saved .tiff/.jpg images for subsequent analysis.

steps.title: Assess and record tissue parameters
steps.instruction: For each tissue image, evaluate and document the following metrics: the percentage of cortex and medulla present; presence (Yes/No) of pyramids; presence (Yes/No) of autolysis; presence (Yes/No) of non‑renal disease such as cancer; glomerular disease severity on a 0 (None) to 3 (Severe) scale; and tubulointerstitial disease severity on a 0 (None) to 3 (Severe) scale.

steps.title: Select kidneys for downstream analysis
steps.instruction: Based on the FFPE assessment, allocate kidneys to the appropriate downstream workflow: • LC‑MS/MS – choose kidneys with low or no glomerular disease and ≥75 % cortex for normal samples, or 100 % tumor tissue for diseased samples. • 3D Imaging – choose kidneys with an approximate 50:50 cortex‑to‑medulla ratio, low or no glomerular disease, and no renal disease.
